description_en: This Bāhāḥ is located in Khācheñ Ṭola between Naka Bahī and Dhalāyacā Ṭola and is a branch of the Hiraṇyavarṇa Mahāvihāra. The stone-paved residential courtyard measures only 3 m x 3.2 m and can be accessed from the north, through an alley underneath a house connecting the courtyard with the Swotha street. The courtyard has a uniquecaityaat its center. It is one of a kind in Patan since itsgarbhagṛha, harmikā, trayodaśabhuvanaand pinnacle are all made of crystal.To the east of the Caitya, is a traditional door which still remains within the modern house fabric. The special carved timber door (missing the threshold) with an extended lintel must have been an entry to a special place related to the rituals but at present, the space is rented for commercial use.The shrine of the main deity of the Bāhāḥ is lost, and a space to the west is still empty waiting for the deity, an east-facing Akṣobhya Buddha, to return from theguthimember who took it to his home when the adjacent house was demolished.An inscription informs that Jayānanda built the Caitya in 1801 CE (NS 921). According to local informants, Jayānanda Śākya was a professional sculptor who used to make images of crystal. This crystal Caitya sits on a copper pedestal, which is shaped as a lotus with three folds of petals turned upwards. This lotus sits on a slim base that gently increases in circumference as it nears the ground. Beneath this is a double-tier rectangular stone plinth. Thecaityais framed by a five-tier copper pinnacle, which is supported by four copper serpents, with their tails near the top and their heads facing downwards. It is encased in a metal cage and has a brass roof. Above the pinnacle is an unbrella (chatra) with five layers and which is supported bystylised snakes(nāga). There are four images in the four corners of the Caitya . In the southwest corner is an image of the donor (Jayānanda), and in the southeast corner is an image of Garuḍa. Similarly, in the northwest corner there is an image of an elephant, and in the northeast corner there is an image of a lion.
description_ne: यो बाहाः खाछेँ टोलमा नक बही र धलायचा टोलको बीचमा रहेको छ । निजी घरको मूल ढोकाबाट भित्र पसेपछि अँध्यारो छिँडीभित्र यो विहार रहेको छ । यो विहार हिरण्यवर्ण महाविहारको शाखा हो । वर्तमानमा यहाँ विहारको नाममा एउटा चैत्य मात्र रहेको छ । चैत्यको गर्भगृहदेखि माथिको सबै भाग स्फटिकले बनाइएको छ । चैत्यको स्थापना गर्ने जयानन्दको पुर्ख्यौली पेशा स्फटिकको कलाकृति बनाउनु थियो । त्यसैले जयानन्दले स्फटिकको चैत्य बनाएका थिए भन्ने स्थानीयको भनाइ छ । चैत्यको पश्चिमतिर डबली जस्तो सानो ठाउँ छोडिएको छ । उक्त खाली ठाउँमा क्वाःपाःद्यःको रूपमा पूर्वाभिमुख अक्षोभ्य बुद्ध राखिएको थियो । नयाँ घर निर्माण गर्दा क्वाःपाःद्यःलाई अन्तै घरमा सारिएको थियो । उक्त रिक्त स्थानमा आजसम्म पनि क्वाःपाःद्यः राखिएको छैन ।यो विहार कहिले निर्माण गरिएको भन्ने थाहा पाईँदैन, तर चैत्यमा राखिएको अभिलेख अनुसार नेसं ९२१ मा जयानन्दले उक्त चैत्य स्थापना गरेका थिए । यो विहार पनि त्यसै समयमा स्थापना गरिएको हुनुपर्छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Aguthiwas established by Jayānanda, his wife Candra Lakṣmī and their son Pṛthvīpati when the Caitya was consecrated for annual worship. Theguthidonated 4ropanīland in Mhayakhu, and 3ropanīin Balama.
